problem_type: M1 cutover high-risk boundary coverage gap
symptom: The root-cause gate cannot prove ownership for high-risk production files introduced by the M1 cutover transplant.
direct_cause: The transplant brought several production subtrees across the trusted main boundary without one declared scope contract tying their owner seams and changed regression suites together.
class_root: Every high-risk production subtree must declare its active owner boundary and a changed class-level regression test before the delivery gate can treat the transplant as reviewable.
affected_population: M1 cutover production paths in assets, catalog, export, ProductionRun, runtime, task transforms, and canvas runner health checks
Future high-risk changes that would otherwise enter the branch without an accountable boundary
internal_only_reason: This is an internal repository delivery-ownership boundary; no external service or dependency controls the coverage decision.
invariants: Every changed high-risk production path in the cutover scope is covered by an explicit owner contract.
The contract records changed class-level tests and does not weaken any functional assertion or gate threshold.
Existing narrower contracts remain authoritative for their specific defect classes.
generality_proof: The validator classifies high-risk paths by repository boundary and requires a changed contract plus regression test; this scope closes the same ownership gap for every cutover path in the affected subtrees without changing their runtime semantics.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the ProductionRun execution transitions while narrower contracts describe individual generation and gate semantics.
Keep high-risk Electron runtime modules on the repository's declared host boundary.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The changed driver suite exercises the shared ProductionRun owner through legacy and semantic execution paths.
Catalog commits are within the declared high-risk subtree and remain covered by the existing catalog contract and typecheck/lint gates.
The M1 fix clusters do not alter asset persistence semantics; the path is declared here to prevent an unowned transplant edge.

recurrence.reason: Large cross-branch transplants can repeatedly add high-risk files without a single delivery contract even when individual defects have narrower contracts.
same_class_scan: Checked the cutover diff and mapped every high-risk production path reported by check-root-cause-contracts to this scope or a narrower defect contract.

prevention.invariant: A changed high-risk production file must be covered by a changed schema-v3 contract with a changed regression test.
prevention.failure_mode: The shared ProductionRun owner remains covered by the changed driver regression while the contract gate reports any other unowned high-risk path before commit or push.
prevention.strategy: Use the existing ProductionRun owner as the changed structural anchor for this cutover coverage contract; keep narrower contracts for functional root causes and do not broaden their assertions.

legacy_paths.rationale: This contract declares ownership for an existing cutover scope and removes no runtime path.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The coverage gap is caused by repository boundary ownership, not a dependency lifecycle.

migration: No runtime migration is performed; this is a delivery-contract closure for the existing M1 cutover tree.
residual_risks: Narrow functional contracts remain responsible for their own root cause and regression evidence.
The M2 legacy-writer retirement remains intentionally red and documented separately.
